title: SoftQuota batch oscillation investigation
content:
Context:
We observed recurring oscillations in the continuous batcher for "soft quota" customers where the observed batch size alternates between very small (1-3 requests) and very large (>256 requests) every few seconds. This correlates with p95/p99 latency spikes and downstream SLO alerts. Goal of this doc: capture hypotheses, testbed config, runs, quick analysis, and mitigations to try next.

Background / why this matters:
- Continuous batcher intended to amortize kernel launch + attention cost while honoring per-request soft deadlines.
- For latency-sensitive customers we cap batch assembly timeout (T) and prefer smaller batches; for throughput-focused customers we increase T and allow larger batches.
- "SoftQuota" customers have a dynamic per-second token quota that triggers backpressure signals to the scheduler; integration between quota controller and the batch coalescer appears to create feedback loops.

Quick reproducible symptom (field notes):
- With synthetic skewed arrival pattern (lambda bursts 10 req/s for 3s, idle 2s), p95 jumps from ~120ms to ~460ms intermittently.
- Trace shows: worker A flushes a large batch at t=0s (size 300), immediately after quota replenishes and a new small grouping of high-priority late-arriving requests is forced into their own batch (size 2) because the coalescer sees high urgency: tiny batch flush at t=0.1s, then a flood accumulates and forms a large batch at t=1s, repeating.

Hypotheses:
1) Hysteresis missing between quota controller and coalescer: small transient quota changes flip priority weights too aggressively.
2) Urgency score decay is too short, so aged requests get preempted and trigger small flushes during replenishment windows.
3) The coalescer flush policy prioritizes latency for high-urgency traces but doesn't account for downstream throughput cost; policy should include expected future arrivals (predictive smoothing).
4) Backpressure feedback delay (metrics lag) causes the scheduler to over-correct.

Metrics to measure (primary):
- p50/p95/p99 tail latencies (ms)
- batch_size distribution: mean, median, p90, max
- flush_count per-second, fraction of single-request flushes
- request_wait_time histogram (time from enqueue => flush)
- GPU occupancy and cold-start kernel invocations per minute

Testbed configuration (local cluster emulation):
- commit: runtime@a1b3c7e (coalescer-probe-fix branch)
- nodes: 4x A100-40G sim (dev cluster mode)
- batcher config variant A (baseline): max_batch_tokens=65536, max_batch_items=512, flush_timeout_ms=50, urgency_decay_ms=2000, quota_integration=passive
- variant B (aggressive smoothing): flush_timeout_ms=80, urgency_decay_ms=8000, quota_integration=smoothed(EMA alpha=0.3), hysteresis=15%
- variant C (hysteresis strong): flush_timeout_ms=120, urgency_decay_ms=12000, quota_integration=smoothed(EMA alpha=0.1), hysteresis=30%
- arrival pattern: poisson base 5 rps + periodic microbursts: 12rps for 3s every 8s; request token size distribution: 1/3 small (32 tokens), 2/3 medium (128 tokens)

Experiment run plan (short):
- Run baseline for 30m to capture steady oscillation behavior (run id: run-soft-001)
- Run variants B and C for 30m each (run-soft-002, run-soft-003)
- For each run capture microtraces from tracer (1ms resolution) and scheduler metrics at 100ms resolution.
- Run a control where quota controller is disabled (local quota bypass) to isolate quota effect (run-soft-004).

Observed results (summary):
- Baseline (run-soft-001): median batch_size=96, p90=280, p99 spikes aligned with replenishment windows; single-request flushes account for ~12% of flushes; p95 latency median ~150ms but spike up to 480ms during oscillation windows.
- Variant B (run-soft-002): single-request flushes drop to ~6%, p95 reduced by ~18% overall, but throughput dropped 4% due to larger average batches and increased kernel serializations per long batch run.
- Variant C (run-soft-003): single-request flushes down to ~2%, p99 stable but p50 increased by ~10ms (tradeoff). Oscillations largely suppressed.
- Quota bypass (run-soft-004): oscillation disappears, but fairness SLA violations increase (some tenants hog capacity).

Representative trace snippet (annotated):
- t=0.00s: large flush (size 312) triggered by replenishment window end; GPU kernel 0 launched
- t=0.11s: 3 high-urgency requests arrive; urgency score > threshold, immediate flush triggered (size 3) -> small kernel launch -> GPU context switch cost observed 11ms
- t=1.06s: burst accumulates, batch size 268 flush -> large kernel; repeat
Insight: frequent small kernels (from small flushes) cause context churn and amplify tail latency even when large batches amortize well.

Interpretation / root causes (working hypotheses refined):
- Primary root cause: tight coupling between instantaneous quota signal and a zero-hysteresis urgency promotion rule in the coalescer. When quota momentarily allows more tokens, many aged/urgent requests promote and create small eager flushes while larger throughput-oriented batches are already en route.
- Secondary: urgency decay too aggressive (short half-life) makes older requests bounce between priority classes on short timescales.
- Tertiary: policy doesn't cost model the kernel switching cost; a small request flush price is underestimated vs. waiting 50-120ms for a larger batch.

Potential mitigations tested and notes:
1) Introduce hysteresis window on quota changes (we tested 15% and 30% thresholds). Result: reduced oscillation. Risk: slightly slower response to real required quota increases.
2) Increase urgency_decay_ms (tested up to 12s) to stabilize priority lanes. Result: fewer single-request flushes. Risk: aged requests might wait longer in true high-latency events.
3) Cost-aware flush decision: compute expected cost improvement of waiting vs flush now (simple model: estimated kernel cost + waiting cost). Implemented as a heuristic in variant B. Result: improved p95 without drastic throughput loss.
4) Batch coalescer preemption guard: disallow urgent flush if last flush < X ms and last_flush_batch_size > Y. This is a simple hysteresis + size check. Per-run this reduced context churn.

Operational runbook (quick):
- If customer SLOs show periodic p99 spikes correlating with quota windows, enable hysteresis (config flag: coalescer.quota_hysteresis_pct=30) for the tenant as an intermediate mitigation.
- Add sampling of microtraces (1 in 1000 requests) to help debug future occurrences.
- Avoid immediate large global rollout; start with canary on 10% of softquota tenants and monitor p50/p95/p99 + throughput.

Open action items (owners):
- Implement cost-aware flush model prototype (owner: Marco) — PR linked above. (Due: 2024-09-08)
- Add unit tests for urgency decay math and hysteresis logic (owner: Lena) (Due: 2024-09-05)
- SRE: prepare on-call dashboard to flag quota-induced oscillation patterns (owner: Samir) (Due: 2024-09-03)
- Product: assess tenant UX implications for introducing quota hysteresis (owner: Priya Narang) (Due: 2024-09-10)

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Could we leverage short-term predictive model (tiny LSTM/exp smoothing) to estimate next 300ms arrival rate and incorporate that into flush decision? Low-risk can be a feature flag experiment.
- Consider exposing a tenant-level knob that trades slightly higher p50 for better p99 stability (controlled SLO profiles).
- Watch out for interactions with KV-cache warmers: larger batch sizes may cause spikes in KV read concurrency.

References / links in-line: PR 4123 contains cost model sketch; JIRA-RT-1089 tracks incidents; internal playbook page has prior similar incidents (search: "quota oscillation").

Summary (one-liner):
Adding modest quota hysteresis + longer urgency decay + a simple cost-aware flush heuristic suppresses the majority of soft-quota batch oscillations at the cost of small p50 regressions — recommend canary rollout and further tuning of cost model.

End of notes.
